title: Discounting under competitive pressure is anti-correlated with winning
finding: In Competitor Displacement deals, lost deals had an average discount of 22.8% vs 4.2% in won deals. Higher discounts did not improve win rates — they may signal that reps are conceding price when they should be competing on value.
implication: Consider tightening discount approval in competitive deals and investing the saved margin in accelerated technical validation instead.

title: Exec Vacuum hits Enterprise hardest among lost deals
finding: 48% of lost Enterprise deals show Exec Vacuum behavioral signals, compared with SMB (40%) and Mid-Market (44%). Enterprise Exec Vacuum deals look legitimate on paper (VP-level champion, multi-stakeholder) but the true economic buyer sits one or two levels above — reps overestimate champion authority.
implication: Enterprise deal reviews should require named economic-buyer engagement before Proposal Sent, not at Negotiation.

title: Enterprise has the highest rate of misattributed loss reasons
finding: 28.2% of Enterprise lost deals have a stated loss reason that contradicts the behavioral evidence. This is higher than other segments, suggesting Enterprise reps are more likely to default to 'price' or 'timing' without accurately diagnosing why the deal actually failed.
implication: Loss reason analysis for this segment is systematically unreliable. CRM-based competitive intelligence from this segment may be misleading.
